steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Claude sometimes changes things differently from what you asked. Sometimes you ask for the wrong thing, too. Today you'll practise undoing a change before you ever need to.

There are three layers of safety.

  1. Before allowing: Deny on the permission card (from Desktop 2)
  2. After allowing: ask Claude to "undo that"
  3. In advance: make a copy of important files
  • Time: 10–15 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 5 (todo.txt in the Practice folder)

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html:
1. Claude app → Code tab → + New.
  2. Check that the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual. (If you switched modes in Desktop 5, switch back to Manual!)

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual (or Ask permissions).

steps.title: Make a copy before changing anything
steps.html:
The surest safety net is a copy. Even if the original gets messed up, you can bring it back from the copy.

Send the sentence below, read the permission card and click Allow. (Instead of a create-file card you may see a run-command card. If the description says it's copying, allow it.)
steps.alt: A permission card for creating todo_backup.txt, a copy of todo.txt

check.q: Is there a todo_backup.txt in the Practice folder now?

steps.title: If you don't see the copy
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • If the folder window was already open, close it and open it again.
  • You can also ask Claude, "What files are in the Practice folder?"

steps.title: Change it oddly on purpose
steps.html:
To practise undoing, something has to change first. Let's put a ★ in front of every line on purpose.

  1. Send the sentence below, read the permission card and click Allow.
  2. Open todo.txt to check the ★s, then close Notepad.
steps.code: Put a ★ at the start of every line in todo.txt

check.q: Is there a ★ at the start of each line in todo.txt?

steps.title: If the ★s weren't added
steps.html:
• You may have denied it, or Claude asked something. Answer it or send it again.
  • If Notepad was already open, close it and open it again.

steps.title: Ask Claude to undo it
steps.html:
Just say this in the same chat. Claude remembers what it changed in this chat.

Undoing also shows a permission card. If the red lines have the ★s and the green lines are the originals, click Allow.
steps.alt: Asking to undo shows a permission card that removes the ★s

check.q: Did the ★s disappear and everything go back to how it was?

steps.title: If it didn't go back: restore from the copy
steps.html:
This is exactly why you made a copy. Say this:

"Restore todo.txt from todo_backup.txt"

Read the permission card and allow it, and the file will match the copy.

steps.title: (Optional) Try typing /undo
steps.html:
Claude Code has a menu that rolls Claude's file edits back to an earlier point. Type /undo (or /rewind) in the box and press {{enterkey}}.

Depending on your desktop app version, this menu may not exist. That's fine. Asking it to undo, plus keeping a copy, is enough.

steps.title: How to read the undo menu
steps.html:
In the menu you pick an earlier point in the chat and decide what to roll back.

Restore codeOnly the files, to that point
Restore conversationOnly the chat, to that point
Restore code and conversationBoth
Never mindCancel

You've already undone it, so close it with Never mind (or Esc).

steps.title: Some things are hard to undo
steps.html:
Claude's edits to file contents are fairly easy to undo. But these can be hard:

  • Files deleted by a command: they may not go to the Recycle Bin. That's why Desktop 4 said to deny rm and del.
  • Files moved or renamed by a command: the undo menu doesn't track them. Ask Claude, "Move it back where it was."
  • Work from other chats or edits you made yourself: Claude may not know about them.
Always copy important files first. With that one habit, most mistakes are nothing to worry about.

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop practice 6 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Now you can undo mistakes, which makes it much easier to hand things over.

Before allowingDeny on the permission card
After allowingIn the same chat: "Undo what you just did"
In advanceCopy important files first ("Copy X to X_backup")
/undoAn undo menu, depending on the app (use it if you have it)

Two things to remember

  1. Ask to undo in the same chat. A new chat doesn't know what was changed.
  2. Commands like delete and move are hard to undo. Read those cards extra carefully before allowing.
